## Idea

Choosing a single combination of parameters (number of PCs, number of
neighbours `k` and resolution) is arbitrary: with a different combination
the clusters change. `coclustR` runs the clustering with **every**
combination of a parameter grid and keeps what is reproducible:

1. **Grid**: Leiden (or Louvain) on Seurat-style SNN graphs for each
   `n_dims × k × resolution` combination.
2. **Meta-barcodes**: cells with exactly the same labels in every run are
   grouped together (they are indistinguishable for the consensus).
3. **Co-clustering matrix**: fraction of runs in which two meta-barcodes
   fall in the same cluster.
4. **Unstable filter**: meta-barcodes with a small, weakly co-clustered
   "core" are flagged as `Unstable`.
5. **Consensus**: hierarchical tree on `1 - co-clustering`, cut with
   `dynamicTreeCut` (`Hybrid` and `DynamicTree` methods).

This vignette uses a `SingleCellExperiment` object;
`vignette("coclustR-seurat")` does the same with Seurat.

```{r libs}
library(coclustR)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(scuttle)
library(scater)
```

## Simulated data

`simulate_sc_counts()` generates negative-binomial counts with known
populations. By design:

* `Pop1` and `Pop2` share 60 % of their marker genes (hard to separate);
* `Pop5` is small (60 cells) and very distinct: a **rare cell type**.

```{r simulate}
sim <- simulate_sc_counts(n_cells = c(400, 300, 250, 150, 60), seed = 1)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = sim$counts),
                            colData = sim$cell_data)
sce
table(sce$population)
```

Standard preprocessing: normalisation, PCA and UMAP.

```{r preprocess}
sce <- logNormCounts(sce)
set.seed(1)
sce <- runPCA(sce, ncomponents = 30)
sce <- runUMAP(sce, dimred = "PCA")
plotReducedDim(sce, "UMAP", colour_by = "population")
```

## Parallelisation

`coclustR` uses the **future** framework but **never changes the plan**:
you choose it before running. Results are identical with any plan for a
given `seed`.

```{r plan, eval = FALSE}
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)
options(future.globals.maxSize = 6 * 1024^3)
```

In this vignette we run sequentially:

```{r plan-seq}
future::plan(future::sequential)
```

## Step 1: clustering grid

This is the slowest step; it is worth saving it (`saveRDS(grid, ...)`) so
the consensus can be repeated with other parameters without recomputing it.
Here we use a reduced grid (3 × 3 × 6 = 54 runs); the package defaults
give 5 × 7 × 14 = 490 runs.

```{r grid}
grid <- run_clustering_grid(
  sce,
  reduction   = "PCA",
  n_dims      = c(10, 20, 30),
  k           = c(10, 20, 30),
  resolutions = seq(0.2, 1.2, 0.2),
  algorithm   = "leiden",
  silhouette  = TRUE,   # optional, slower
  seed        = 11,
  verbose     = FALSE
)
grid
head(grid$metrics)
```

`grid$labels` is a cells × runs matrix with the labels of every run.

### Grid diagnostics

Number of clusters (colour and text) and modularity (size) for each
combination:

```{r overview, fig.height = 4}
plot_grid_overview(grid)
```

Metrics as a function of resolution, one line per `k`:

```{r metrics, fig.height = 6}
plot_grid_metrics(grid)
```

Plateaus (the number of clusters does not change as the resolution
increases) usually correspond to real structure. The silhouette almost
always decreases with resolution, so parameters should not be chosen based
on it alone.

## Step 2: consensus

`run_coclustering()` adds the `coclust_Hybrid` and `coclust_DynamicTree`
columns to `colData` and stores the full result in
`metadata(sce)$coclustR`. We pass the pre-computed grid with `grid =`.

`min_cluster_size` counts **meta-barcodes**, not cells. In real data, with
thousands of meta-barcodes, 50 is reasonable; this simulation has few of
them (clusters are very reproducible), so we use 20.

```{r consensus}
sce <- run_coclustering(
  sce,
  grid                = grid,
  stability_threshold = 0.5,
  min_core_cells      = 50,
  min_core_stability  = 0.8,
  linkage             = "complete",
  min_cluster_size    = 20,
  rescue_min_cells    = 50
)
res <- get_coclust_result(sce)
res
```

Comparison with the simulated populations:

```{r compare}
table(population = sce$population, Hybrid = sce$coclust_Hybrid)
table(population = sce$population, DynamicTree = sce$coclust_DynamicTree)
```

Is the consensus better than a single run? We compare the adjusted Rand
index (ARI) of the consensus with that of each of the 54 runs:

```{r ari, fig.height = 3.5}
ari <- function(x) bluster::pairwiseRand(sce$population, x, mode = "index")
ari_runs <- apply(grid$labels, 2, ari)
ari_hybrid <- ari(sce$coclust_Hybrid)

summary(ari_runs)
ari_hybrid

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data.frame(ARI = ari_runs), aes(ARI)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ari_hybrid, colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "ARI of each run (grey) vs Hybrid consensus (red)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Here both methods agree. In general `DynamicTree` is more conservative: when
two populations overlap (such as `Pop1` and `Pop2`) it leaves many of their
cells as `Unstable`, whereas `Hybrid` assigns them (its PAM step sends each
meta-barcode to the closest cluster). `Hybrid` is usually the recommended
option; `DynamicTree` is useful to see which cores are the most solid (the
Seurat vignette shows that difference).

## Visualisation

Consensus clusters on the UMAP (works the same with Seurat objects):

```{r umap, fig.height = 4}
plot_clusters_embedding(sce, color_by = c("coclust_Hybrid",
                                          "coclust_DynamicTree",
                                          "population"))
```

Diagnostic of the unstable filter: each point is a meta-barcode; unstable
ones are those below and to the left of the lines (`min_core_cells`,
`min_core_stability`).

Core stability is computed **excluding the meta-barcode itself**, so an
isolated meta-barcode (one that does not co-cluster ≥ `stability_threshold`
with any other) has stability 0 and sits at the bottom of the plot. If it
has at least `min_core_cells` cells it is kept (this is the case of `Pop5`:
a distinct population that always clusters together); otherwise it is
flagged as unstable. In other words, `min_core_cells` also acts as the
**minimum detectable population size**: lower it if you are looking for
rarer cell types.

```{r stability, fig.height = 4}
plot_stability(sce)
```

Co-clustering matrix on a sample of cells, stratified by sample and cluster,
annotated with any `colData` column:

```{r heatmap, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 7}
plot_coclustering_heatmap(sce, n_cells = 500,
                          stratify_by = c("Sample", "Hybrid"),
                          annotate_by = c("Sample", "population"))
```

If ComplexHeatmap is not installed, `engine = "ggplot"` gives a simple
version.

## Tuning the consensus without re-running the grid

`coclust_from_grid()` repeats only the consensus (seconds). For example, to
see the effect of the **rescue of stable populations**: `Pop5` is so
distinct that all of its cells get the same labels in every run, so it
collapses into **a single meta-barcode**. Without the rescue,
dynamicTreeCut cannot turn a single meta-barcode into a cluster:

```{r rescue}
no_rescue <- coclust_from_grid(grid, min_cluster_size = 20,
                               rescue_min_cells = NULL, verbose = FALSE)
table(population = sce$population, Hybrid = no_rescue$cell_clusters$Hybrid)
```

`Pop5` ends up as `Unstable`, so does `Pop4` (also very reproducible), and
the PAM step of Hybrid even places `Pop3` in the same cluster as `Pop1`.
With `rescue_min_cells = 50` (the default) each of them is recovered as its
own cluster.

Other parameters that can be explored this way: `linkage` (`"average"`,
`"ward.D2"`), `deep_split`, `min_cluster_size`, `min_cluster_cells`,
`stability_threshold`.

```{r deep}
deep <- coclust_from_grid(grid, min_cluster_size = 20, deep_split = 2,
                          methods = "hybrid", verbose = FALSE)
table(population = sce$population, Hybrid = deep$cell_clusters$Hybrid)
```

To store an alternative version in the object, use a different prefix:

```{r store-alt}
sce <- run_coclustering(sce, grid = grid, min_cluster_size = 20,
                        linkage = "average", prefix = "coclustAvg_",
                        verbose = FALSE)
grep("coclust", colnames(colData(sce)), value = TRUE)
```

(The full result stored in `metadata(sce)$coclustR` is always the one from
the last call.)

## Low-level functions

Each step of the pipeline is available separately:

```{r lowlevel}
mb    <- collapse_metabarcodes(grid$labels)            # meta-barcodes
co    <- coclustering_matrix(mb$labels)                # consensus matrix
stab  <- core_stability(co, mb$sizes, threshold = 0.5)
unst  <- flag_unstable(stab, min_core_cells = 50, min_core_stability = 0.8)
cons  <- consensus_clusters(co[!unst, !unst], mb$sizes[!unst],
                            min_cluster_size = 20)

c(cells = ncol(sce), metabarcodes = nrow(mb$labels), unstable = sum(unst))
head(cons$labels)
```
